iptime-ip-camera-isolation-nox-vms.title: How to Isolate Chinese IP Cameras from the Internet and Use Them Safely with NOX
iptime-ip-camera-isolation-nox-vms.description: A practical guide to securing Chinese-made IP cameras: block camera internet access with ipTime egress rules and put NOX VMS in front as the single, TLS-protected entry point — without replacing existing cameras.
faq: I only used a P2P app (XMEye, Hik-Connect). If I block the camera, won't that app stop working?

Yes, and that is the intended result. The app worked because the camera kept a two-way connection to the manufacturer's cloud at every moment, and this guide exists precisely to cut that connection. NOX VMS provides the same functions (remote viewing, alerts, recording) through a single authenticated, TLS-protected path.
Can I come in over a VPN instead of port forwarding?

That is the safer option. Connecting to NOX as if on the LAN through ipTime's VPN server or WireGuard reduces the attack surface compared with port forwarding. Consider the operational burden, though: every staff member must install and manage the VPN.
Does this work on routers other than ipTime?

The principle is the same. ASUS, Netgear, TP-Link, and ISP-provided routers all offer a similar feature under names such as "Access Control" or "Outbound Firewall". Only the menu names differ; the action — block outbound traffic from this internal IP — is the same.
If RTSP/ONVIF is blocked, won't NOX lose access to the cameras too?
NOX talks to the cameras inside the isolated network. The ipTime egress rule only blocks the camera-to-internet direction; NOX-to-camera traffic on the same LAN is not affected.
